messages:
Anya: heads-up — bringing compact-ranker v0.9 (4-bit PTQ build) onto staging for a quick quality smoke. noticing a small MRR dip vs baseline on short queries. sharing numbers below.

EvalBot: offline eval snapshot for compact-v0.9-ptq-int4 -> baseline float32
EvalBot: NDCG@10: 0.842 -> 0.835 (-0.007)
EvalBot: MRR@10: 0.611 -> 0.576 (-0.035)  <-- most of the lift lost on short (<=3 token) queries

Miguel: hmm that's a larger MRR delta than i'd expect. are we sure the eval harness preproc is identical? whitespace/tokenization differences can wreck short query signal.

Priya: can you paste an example short query that degraded? also any formatting differences between train/dev vs eval corpus?

Anya: example from holdout (degraded):
Anya: "how to resetpassword"  (appears to include a NUL in original capture)
Anya: another: "what’s the ETAfor release" (looks like a zero-width or weird whitespace char between token and punctuation)

Sam: whoa zero bytes/ZWSPs could change token boundaries for our tokenizer and push priming tokens earlier/later. we should run a simple normalization check (NFKC + remove control chars) on the eval set and compare.

Priya: agreed. quick sanity script I use:
Priya: ```python
Priya: import unicodedata, re
Priya: def clean(s):
Priya:     s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
Priya:     s = re.sub(r'\x00|\z|[\u200B-\u200D]', '', s)
Priya:     return s.strip()
Priya: ```

Miguel: also confirm token offsets for compact tokenizer: run tokenization on raw vs cleaned and diff offsets for the problematic queries.

Anya: ran token diff on 50 failing examples locally — ~68% had different token splits after cleaning. looks suspiciously correlated with the worst drops.

EvalBot: quick re-eval with cleaned queries (NFKC + control char removal) on same model:
EvalBot: NDCG@10: 0.842 -> 0.839
EvalBot: MRR@10: 0.611 -> 0.602
EvalBot: (MRR drop reduced from -0.035 to -0.009)

Sam: OK that narrows it to preprocessing differences. two follow ups:
Sam: 1) ensure training/pretraining corpus used same normalization (check ingest pipeline)
Sam: 2) for quant path, test int8 per-channel vs per-tensor kernels — weird token boundary shifts can amplify quant noise on short sequences.

Miguel: for (2) i can spin a quick PTQ sweep tomorrow morning. command i ran for staging eval:
Miguel: ```bash
Miguel: python tools/eval.py --model compact-v0.9-ptq-int4 --dataset holdout --limit 10000 --batch 256
Miguel: ```

Priya: small note: our logger truncates query display at 64 chars and hides nonprintables. let's add an encoded field in eval output with hex of original bytes so we can triage weird whitespace reliably.

Anya: matches what i saw. i'll open a tiny PR to add hex_encoded_query to the eval CSV and a flag --normalize-preproc (off by default) so we can compare apples-to-apples during bringup.

DeployBot: deployment complete: compact-v0.9-ptq-int4 -> staging (tag: build-2026-02-03-compact)

Priya: after PR lands, run a 100k-sample re-eval with cleaned vs raw to estimate population impact. if delta disappears we ship the normalization into preprocess of the serving stack; otherwise continue quant kernel/quantization config investigation.

Anya: plan: (1) PR for logging + normalize flag (today), (2) Miguel runs PTQ kernel sweep (tomorrow), (3) 100k cleaned vs raw eval (Thu) and sync on Friday. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

Sam: +1. please tag me on the PR and drop the eval CSV in #eng-ml when ready so we can slice by query length/priming type.

Anya: will do. filing a quick ticket with the sample pairs and the failing examples so we don't lose them.

Miguel: ping if you want me to re-run with per-channel int8 on the same cleaned dataset — might remove residuals.

Anya: thanks, will take you up on that after PR. closing loop here for now :)
